options.text: The same type with every property made optional
Only the first property of T
The same type with every property made readonly
A union of T's property types

questions.explanation: Partial<T> makes every property optional — ideal for update functions where the caller supplies only the fields to change.

questions.prompt: What's the difference between Pick/Omit and Extract/Exclude?

options.text: They are identical
Pick/Omit select or drop object properties; Extract/Exclude keep or remove members of a union
Pick/Omit work on unions; Extract/Exclude work on objects
All four work only on functions

questions.explanation: Pick/Omit operate on object properties (by key); Extract/Exclude filter members of a union type.

questions.prompt: To build an object type with one boolean per key in 'admin' | 'editor', you write ______<'admin' | 'editor', boolean>. (one word)
questions.explanation: Record<Keys, Value> builds an object type with the given keys and value type, requiring an entry for each key.

questions.prompt: Why is it `ReturnType<typeof makeUser>` and not `ReturnType<makeUser>`?

options.text: makeUser is a reserved word
ReturnType needs the function's type; `typeof makeUser` gives that type from the function value
typeof is required by all utility types
They are equivalent

questions.explanation: makeUser is a value; ReturnType needs a type. The typeof type query converts the value to its type first.

options.text: Promise<string>
string
unknown
void

questions.explanation: Awaited unwraps the value a promise resolves to (including nested promises), so Awaited<Promise<string>> is string.

questions.prompt: Which statements about utility types are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: They keep derived types in sync with their source type
Partial and Readonly are deep by default
They are built into the standard library
Deriving avoids duplicating shapes

questions.explanation: Utility types are built in, keep derived types in sync, and avoid duplication. Partial and Readonly apply one level only — they are not deep.
